subject: inflated lod scores and qtl vs qtlbim

messages.author: c1131b3ecff97dc1
messages.subject: inflated lod scores and qtl vs qtlbim
parts:
Hi. I've been trying to analyze a binary trait with R/QTL, and find the odd result that running a simple Scanone (HK or EM) almost everything is "significant" by permutation tests (even just glancing at the chart, I have LOD scores >6 along almost the entire chromosomes, actually greater than 10 for most loci). Yet if I run qtlbim, I find actual peaks (based on LPD, which the authors suggest is akin to LOD scores, but in their bayesian framework). (Note I'm using the most recent package, R version 2.15 and qtl_1.26-14, and I don't think it's a coding error because I have since downloaded a dataset from a published paper and I can replicate their scanone LOD plots in R/qtl.) I would in this case think that the regular "qtl" package is preferable to "qtlbim" because the latter will not allow analysis of the X chromosome, but is there any suggestion for what could cause inflated LOD scores across the entire chromosome and so differentiate R/qtl from qtlbim? I'm fine with trying most any package (preference for free ones of course), but while we have some issues with the X chromosome that we need to work out, we think the X chromosome is important and so we do want the option of analyzing data from it.

I'll note I am using the MSG software (Andolfatto and Stern's work) to read in conditional probabilities directly, but I think I finally got this to work -- esp as I can replicate the results from one of their published plots.

If someone has time, any suggestions are greatly appreciated, because I'm a bit baffled on how to proceed or what's causing the huge qtl/qtlbim discrepancy.

messages.author: c1131b3ecff97dc1
messages.subject: Re: inflated lod scores and qtl vs qtlbim
parts: Actually I think I just figured it out: inflated LOD scores from missing genotype data coded as 1/2 probability (backcross) in HK or EM, with more typical LOD scores using Marker Regression.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] inflated lod scores and qtl vs qtlbim
parts:
Hi,
Yes; I was using "binary" for the model. Yet I found that altering the method from "em" or "hk" to be "mr" is the only way I can obtain reasonable LOD scores; I assume the inflation with the interval mapping em/hk protocols is due to the way they handle missing genotype data. At least I cannot think of any other explanation for the fact that when I tried the "mr" the LOD scores finally became reasonable, and more closely approximating what qtlbim would yield for the autosomes.

messages.author: c1131b3ecff97dc1
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] inflated lod scores and qtl vs qtlbim
parts:
Yes; I think this is the problem... I'm trying to see if I can alter the calls for missing genotypes and just encode it as missing/NA. The MSG data is imported as as a read cross object with probabilities, bypassing the calc.genoprob step (or rather replacing what rqtl would yield for calc.genoprob with the probabilities from MSG). Unfortunately if I try to manually replace the priors of 0.5 (the missing genotype data, e.g., around telomeres where there is no flanking data to aid in computing the probability of a given genotype), when I try to run scanone with a method other than marker regression (e.g., "hk") I receive the error message "Error: NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 4)."

Yet since this is a backcross (binary trait/model, no covariates, with 100s of markers per chromosome) I'm wondering if Haley-Knot or EM would cause the same problem regardless of whether the MSG input the uncertain data priors as 0.5, given what you note on p97 of your book. " Consider a backcross with genotypes coded as 0 and 1. In Haley–Knott regression, an individual with no genotype data will be treated as if its genotype were 1/2 (and were known to be 1/2). This results in a slightly inflated estimate of the effect of a QTL but also a greatly reduced estimate of the residual variation, and so can give inflated LOD scores."

Then a question becomes whether this causes a problem only with Scanone, or if the problems here will propagate to higher scans (Scantwo, StepwiseQTL...). If you have time, I appreciate your thoughts on this (but I understand in full if you don't have time; thank you for your comments so far).
Thank you,
Hilary

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] inflated lod scores and qtl vs qtlbim
parts: > Yes; I think this is the problem... I'm trying to see if I can alter the calls for missing genotypes and just encode it as missing/NA. The MSG data is imported as as a read cross object with probabilities, bypassing the calc.genoprob step (or rather replacing what rqtl would yield for calc.genoprob with the probabilities from MSG). Unfortunately if I try to manually replace the priors of 0.5 (the missing genotype data, e.g., around telomeres where there is no flanking data to aid in computing the probability of a given genotype), when I try to run scanone with a method other than marker regression (e.g., "hk") I receive the error message "Error: NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 4)."
scanone and other functions can't handle missing values in any of the genotype probabilities.

> Yet since this is a backcross (binary trait/model, no covariates, with 100s of markers per chromosome) I'm wondering if Haley-Knot or EM would cause the same problem regardless of whether the MSG input the uncertain data priors as 0.5, given what you note on p97 of your book. " Consider a backcross with genotypes coded as 0 and 1. In Haley–Knott regression, an individual with no genotype data will be treated as if its genotype were 1/2 (and were known to be 1/2). This results in a slightly inflated estimate of the effect of a QTL but also a greatly reduced estimate of the residual variation, and so can give inflated LOD scores."
That discussion concerns selective genotyping for a quantitative trait. I wouldn't think there would be a problem with a binary trait; I've not seen problems along those lines.

> Then a question becomes whether this causes a problem only with Scanone, or if the problems here will propagate to higher scans (Scantwo, StepwiseQTL...). If you have time, I appreciate your thoughts on this (but I understand in full if you don't have time; thank you for your comments so far).

If things don't work with scanone, I think it will only get worse in the case of multiple-QTL models.

karl
